residency.test: Resident if France is your home (foyer) or principal place of stay, or your main professional activity is in France, or France is the centre of your economic interests. Any one is enough.
residency.note: Households are taxed together as a foyer fiscal, not individually. This is one of the largest structural differences from Anglo-Saxon systems.

headline.quotient_familial: income is divided by the number of household parts before the scale is applied
headline.social_levies: CSG 9.2% and CRDS 0.5% on 98.25% of salary, on top of contributions
headline.flat_tax: 30% (12.8% income tax + 17.2% social) on most investment income

income_tax.name: Impôt sur le revenu
income_tax.note: half a part per child for the first two, a full part from the third; the benefit per half-part is capped

standard_deduction.name: Abattement de 10% pour frais professionnels
standard_deduction.note: automatic; elect actual expenses (frais réels) instead if they are higher

employer.name: Cotisations patronales (approximate)
employer.note: roughly 25-42% depending on salary level and available reliefs

self_employed.name: Cotisations sociales travailleur indépendant
self_employed.note: approximate blended rate; the micro-entrepreneur regime uses much lower flat rates

surcharges.name: Contribution exceptionnelle sur les hauts revenus
surcharges.note: thresholds double for couples filing jointly

capital_gains.securities: prélèvement forfaitaire unique of 30% (12.8% tax + 17.2% social levies), or elect the progressive scale
capital_gains.real_estate: 19% plus 17.2% social levies, with taper relief - fully exempt after 22 years for income tax and 30 years for social levies
capital_gains.note: the PFU election is made for the whole household and the whole year, not per transaction

quirks: Tax is withheld at source (prélèvement à la source) but you still file an annual declaration; the withholding rate is set from the return you filed a year earlier.
The quotient familial can make a family's effective rate dramatically lower than a single person's on identical income, but the benefit per half-part is capped (around 1,791 per half-part).
Social levies (CSG/CRDS) are not income tax and are not always creditable under treaties - US taxpayers in particular have had long-running disputes about this.
Every household member's income goes on one return. Getting married or entering a PACS mid-year changes the filing unit.
Filing deadlines differ by département, staggered across late May and early June.

reporting.who_must_file: Every fiscal household resident in France, including those with no tax to pay. Non-residents file for French-source income.

deadlines.what: Online declaration for départements 01-19 and non-residents
Paper declaration deadline where paper filing is still permitted
Avis d'imposition issued; balance due or refund paid

forms.name: Foreign bank, crypto and life insurance accounts

documents_to_collect: Numéro fiscal (13 digits) and access to the impots.gouv.fr space
Employer year-end statement and the pre-filled amounts to verify
IFU (imprimé fiscal unique) from banks and brokers
Details of every foreign account held during the year - form 3916 is mandatory and separately penalised
Receipts for childcare, home services and donations

penalties.late_filing: 10% increase, rising to 40% if the return is still not filed 30 days after formal notice
penalties.undeclared_foreign_account: 1,500 per account per year, or 10,000 for accounts in non-cooperative states

sources.name: Barème de l'impôt sur le revenu

warnings: The cap on the quotient familial benefit per half-part is not applied, so results for high-income households with children understate the tax slightly.
Employee contribution rates vary by employer, sector and pension scheme; treat the social security lines as a close approximation.
The décote for low tax amounts and the reduction for modest incomes are not modelled.
